v1.feedback: The moonbow concept lands — a spectral arc sweeping across a differential-growth coral is a legit surprise swerve, not just a palette swap. Two issues: the growth is purely planar (XZ) with only a shallow Y droop from age, so the coral reads as a flat doily from most orbit angles rather than a volumetric reef form; adding even modest Y-axis branching or vertical ruffling would sell the coral read much faster. The spectral band desaturation (0.15 mix toward luma) is the right instinct but the arc width of 0.45 rad is narrow enough that the moonbow can be missed entirely at some rotation angles — widen it to ~0.7 or add a second fainter counter-arc. Finally, 40k render particles on a 4k-vertex skeleton means heavy oversampling; tighten the scatter radius or let particle density track skeleton density so the form stays crisp instead of slightly hazy at full growth.

v2.feedback: The differential growth is genuine and the moonbow spectral arc is a legitimate color swerve, but the coral is fundamentally a flat XZ doily with cosmetic Y ruffles — it reads more as a sea urchin coaster than volumetric coral. Push the ruffling harder (stack multiple growth rings at different Y offsets, or let the growth curve itself climb in Y over time) so the form has real 3D silhouette from the default camera angle. The moonbow sweep is too subtle at 0.55 saturation with additive blending on already-bright particles — consider darkening the base palette slightly in the arc region before injecting the spectrum, so the prismatic band actually reads as a surprise rather than a faint tint you have to squint to catch.
